aarti.tek: Victory, victory to you, Jāharvīr, O Hari; victory, victory to you, the hero Gūgā, O Hari. Coming down to earth, you take away the sorrows of your devotees.
aarti.pad1: Whoever worships with love — yes indeed, with love — his sorrows flee far away, and you remove his obstacles. Giver of all good, you take away the suffering of the body. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: You were called the son of Rāv Jevar, and Queen Bāchal is your mother; the hero was born in Bāgaṛ, and he is hailed with cries of victory. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: You made the vine of dharma grow, and you practise austerity night and day, every day; you punished the wicked, and in the world you remained true. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: You took the vow of truth and non-violence and feared falsehood; holding it wrong to break your word, you left your home. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: You practised austerity in a hermit's hut, and all marvel at it; in all four directions devotees are on their way, and they arrive here full of hope. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: Come into our house, O unshakeable canopy: so saying, the devotees serve; whoever serves with love, his stores of wealth are filled. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: Offering body, mind and wealth, the devotee gains devotion; on the ninth day of the dark half of Bhādoṃ he offers worship and devotion. ॥7॥
